notebooks.title: Foundations of Autonomous Objective Discovery in Artificial Systems
notebooks.summary: Autonomous agents leverage curiosity-driven learning to navigate complex environments, effectively bootstrapping discovery in the presence of deceptive or sparse rewards. PC-PPO and related multi-objective reinforcement learning (MORL) frameworks allow for non-dominated policy maintenance, yet systems remain limited by underlying convexity assumptions in scalarization functions when attempting to self-formulate new research objectives.

Curiosity-driven learning acts as a fundamental bootstrap for exploration, enabling agents to discover skills in complex environments where reward signals are deceptive. [source-feb4fddb33664d63]

Multi-objective reinforcement learning (MORL) frameworks can maintain non-dominated policy portfolios, provided scalarization functions remain within convex bounds. [source-4668e4bd26fe43c7]
notebooks.limitations: Existing mechanisms struggle with long-term, self-directed objective prioritization in non-convex environments, relying heavily on underlying convexity assumptions in scalarization functions.
